summary: Basoko territory (Tshopo province), west of Kisangani along the Congo and Aruwimi rivers, is far from the eastern conflict zones and no armed group is known to hold territory there. The state administers Basoko town and the Basoko, Yalimbongo and Basali secteurs, with the PNC as the main day-to-day security force and limited FARDC presence. Local land, chieftaincy or plantation disputes may occur but are not known to have produced non-state control. Web research was unavailable for this run, so confidence is medium for Basoko town and low for rural villages.

zones.description: Basoko town (territorial headquarters) and adjacent Bolanga/Lokutu area on the Congo-Aruwimi confluence
zones.evidence: Territorial capital with state administration, PNC commissariat and some FARDC/naval presence on the river; no known armed-group activity. No web sources could be retrieved in this run (search budget exhausted, search engines blocked), so the assessment rests on the absence of known armed-group activity in Basoko territory.

zones.description: Rural villages of Basoko secteur, Yalimbongo and Basali (Aruwimi/Lomami forest and ex-plantation areas)
zones.evidence: Remote river and forest villages with no reported non-state armed control; order kept by PNC posts and customary chiefs under state administration. No web sources could be retrieved in this run (search budget exhausted, search engines blocked), so the assessment rests on the absence of known armed-group activity in Basoko territory.
